# Incident Report — MTA 2025-01-22 PCAP Forensics

## Scope
Evidence reviewed: `2025-01-22-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (39,427 frames, 26.1 MB, capture duration 3,202 seconds / ~53 min). No separate IDS/Suricata export was present in the evidence directory — all findings below are derived directly from packet analysis with `tshark`. No internet lookups were performed.

## 1. Infected Host

| Attribute | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.1.17.215** | Dominant host in all conversations; DHCP client |
| MAC address | **00:d0:b7:26:4a:74** (Intel NIC) | ARP / DHCP / Ethernet source |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ** | DHCP Option 12; NBNS Workstation/Server registrations; Kerberos SPN |
| AD domain | BLUEMOONTUESDAY.COM (DC: WIN-GSH54QLW48D.bluemoontuesday.com, 10.1.17.2) | DNS SRV/CLDAP/dynamic DNS update traffic |
| Logged-in user | **shutchenson** (BLUEMOONTUESDAY\shutchenson) | Kerberos AS-REQ `CNameString` |

## 2. Malware Family and Attribution Confidence

**Family: ClickFix-delivered PowerShell backdoor, followed by a Quasar/AsyncRAT-style .NET RAT channel (self-signed TLS on a custom port), with legitimate TeamViewer subsequently abused for hands-on-keyboard access.**

**Attribution basis: behavioral / TTP-based, not signature-confirmed.** No AV/YARA/IDS signature hits are available in this evidence set — there is no separate alert export, and no static detection was run. The family name above is inferred purely from the observed traffic pattern:

- A fake "Google/verification" lure page → clipboard-paste execution → `mshta`-style fetch of a VBScript "scriptlet" component → hidden PowerShell that beacons using the victim's **C: drive volume serial number (converted to decimal) as its bot ID** — this exact loader logic and beaconing convention is characteristic of ClickFix campaigns.
- The stager subsequently drives the host to open a second TLS channel to two different IPs, each presenting a **self-signed TLS certificate whose Common Name is literally the server's own IP address**, on a non-standard port (2917) and on 443 — a hallmark of Quasar-derived RATs (AsyncRAT/DcRAT/VenomRAT/QuasarRAT all use `SslStream` with a self-signed cert exactly this way).
- The malware then silently deploys a genuine, unmodified copy of **TeamViewer** for direct hands-on-keyboard remote access.

No ransomware deployment or file-encryption activity is visible in this capture; it ends mid-RAT-session.

## 3. Infection Timeline (relative to capture start)

| t (s) | Event |
|---|---|
| 0–31 | Normal Windows/Edge boot telemetry and a Bing search session (benign baseline) |
| 38.19 | DNS query: `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` → 104.21.x.1 (Cloudflare) — fake Google Authenticator verification lure |
| 38.86 | DNS query: `authenticatoor.org` → **82.221.136.26** — ClickFix gate/TDS |
| 52.29 | DNS query: `appointedtimeagriculture.com` → 217.70.186.109 (TLS 443) — intermediate redirect hop |
| 58.27 | `checkappexec.microsoft.com` queried — Windows SmartScreen reputation check fires (consistent with the user pasting/running a command) |
| 60.30 | `GET http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872` — HTTP/1.1, UA `Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; …)` (mshta.exe's default UA). Server: Node.js/Express. Returns a 417-byte VBScript "sct" component (SHA256 below) that opens **`https://azure.microsoft.com`** as a decoy tab while launching hidden PowerShell |
| 61.90 | DNS for `azure.microsoft.com` confirms the decoy tab opened |
| 62.15 | `GET /api/file/get-file/29842.ps1` — obfuscated Base64/`IEX` PowerShell stager downloaded |
| 62.37 onward | Backdoor beacon loop begins: `GET http://5.252.153.241/1517096937` every ~5.2 s (**588 requests** logged over the full capture) |
| 124.99–129.21 | C2 instructs download of `TeamViewer`, `Teamviewer_Resource_fr`, `TV`, `pas.ps1`; beacon reports back `k=message = startup shortcut created; status = success` — persistence via Startup-folder shortcut confirmed |
| 611–615 | TeamViewer's legitimate client protocol phones home: `GET http://master16.teamviewer.com/din.aspx?...&client=DynGate` (185.188.32.26) — confirms the dropped TeamViewer binary is genuine and now registering with TeamViewer's real infrastructure |
| 889.6 | First connection to **45.125.66.32:2917**, TLS handshake, self-signed cert CN=`45.125.66.32` — RAT control channel; ~9.6 MB downloaded / 587 KB uploaded over the session, with repeated reconnects at 903s, 912s, 2420s, 2432s, 2441s, 2584s, 2597s, 2605s |
| 917.4 | Parallel/failover connection to **45.125.66.252:443**, same self-signed-cert-to-IP pattern |
| 3202.4 | Capture ends; beacon to 5.252.153.241 still active |

## 4. Indicators of Compromise (all grounded in this capture)

**C2 / malicious endpoints**
- `5.252.153.241:80` — PowerShell stager C2 / payload-hosting gate (Node.js/Express "get-file" API)
- `45.125.66.32:2917` — RAT C2, TLS with self-signed certificate (CN=IP)
- `45.125.66.252:443` — RAT C2 (secondary/failover), TLS with self-signed certificate (CN=IP)
- `82.221.136.26:443` — `authenticatoor.org`, ClickFix gate/TDS

**Malicious / lure domains**
- `authenticatoor.org` (→ 82.221.136.26)
- `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` (→ 104.21.64.1 / .48.1 / .32.1 / .80.1 / .16.1 / .96.1 / .112.1, Cloudflare-fronted)
- `appointedtimeagriculture.com` (→ 217.70.186.109)

**Malicious URLs**
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872`
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1`
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/pas.ps1`
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TeamViewer`
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/Teamviewer_Resource_fr`
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TV`
- `http://5.252.153.241/1517096937` (beacon/bot-ID URI, victim's C:\ drive serial number in decimal)

**Transferred files and SHA256**

| File | SHA256 | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 264872 (VBScript scriptlet) | `c74123dbccded43fda61651e102750b041d4c3af6fda88cd6436f9276653e1` | Stage-1 dropper: opens decoy `azure.microsoft.com` tab, hidden-runs PowerShell |
| 29842.ps1 | `b8ce40900788ea26b9e4c9af7efab533e8d39ed1370da09b93fcf72a16750de` | Obfuscated PowerShell backdoor loop (Base64+`IEX`); decodes to a `while($true)` C2-polling loop keyed on `$fso.GetDrive("c:\").SerialNumber` |
| pas.ps1 | `a833f27c2bb4cad31344e70386c44b5c221f031d7cd2f2a6b8601919e79016` | Same backdoor loop logic as 29842.ps1, re-served |
| TeamViewer | `904280f20d697d876ab90a1b74c0f22a83b859e8b0519cb411fda26f1642f5` | Genuine TeamViewer executable, deployed for hands-on-keyboard access |
| Teamviewer_Resource_fr | `9634ecaf469149379bba80a745f53d823948c41ce4e347860701cbdff69351` | TeamViewer resource DLL |
| TV | `3448da03808f24568e6181011f8521c0713ea6160efd05bff20c43b091ff59` | TeamViewer support-module PE |

## 5. Summary for Remediation
Host **DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ (10.1.17.215)**, logged in as **BLUEMOONTUESDAY\shutchenson**, was compromised via a ClickFix-style fake-verification lure that led to execution of a scripted dropper. This established a persistent PowerShell backdoor (Startup-folder shortcut) polling `5.252.153.241` every ~5 seconds, which in turn opened a self-signed-TLS RAT channel to `45.125.66.32:2917`/`45.125.66.252:443` and silently installed TeamViewer for direct attacker access. The session was still active for the full 53-minute capture with no evidence of ransomware deployment observed in this pcap. Recommend immediate isolation of 10.1.17.215, credential reset for shutchenson, and blocking of all listed IPs/domains at the perimeter.
